claim: For Turing's 1936 'On Computable Numbers' the eye's two channels report citation counts that differ by ~3.2x, each stamped with its own source: openalex/cited_by ~8127 versus Crossref is-referenced-by-count ~2553.

args.query: On Computable Numbers with an Application to the Entscheidungsproblem

upstream_of_record.field: cited_by_count for W2126160338 (doi 10.1112/plms/s2-42.1.230), against crossref message.is-referenced-by-count for the same DOI

notes: Requires two eye calls (the eye_search openalex drill above, plus eye_paper_enrich on the DOI); both are recorded and both were run. This gap is anomalous, not a systematic offset: I measured the same Crossref-vs-OpenAlex pair on nine other classics and they all sit at 1.04-1.53x (Nash 1951 6356/6600=1.04x; Godel 1931 2086/2339=1.12x; Metropolis 1953 29994/37238=1.24x; Watson-Crick 1953 10509/13287=1.26x; Hodgkin-Huxley 1952 17818/23366=1.31x; Einstein 1905 2997/4254=1.42x; Wakefield 1998 1997/2952=1.48x; Black-Scholes 1973 19814/29580=1.49x; Shannon 1948 53454/81805=1.53x). Subject is a deceased historical figure and the fact is a pair of counts.
